title: Attorney General of Massachusetts

context.text: Each nominee was the only name on their party's September 1, 2026 primary ballot: incumbent Democrat Andrea Campbell received 742,871 votes and Republican Michael Walsh 214,932 (official results; other votes were write-ins and blanks).
The Green Papers lists Campbell and Walsh as the only two candidates for attorney general in the November 3, 2026 general election; no independent or third-party candidate is listed.

candidates.name: Andrea Campbell
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the September 1, 2026 Democratic primary.

priorities.text: Making life more affordable, including wage enforcement, junk-fee regulation and actions against utility rate increases, corporate landlords and insulin pricing.
Defending freedoms and funding against federal actions through litigation, including voting rights, immigration, and environmental and housing-program cases.
Expanding housing supply, including enforcement of the MBTA Communities Act and endorsement of Ballot Question 7.

positions.summary: Her campaign says she launched a confidential hotline for abortion care, co-sponsored a shield law for clinicians, and fought to keep mifepristone available through telehealth.
positions.quote: In Massachusetts, reproductive freedom is protected, and Andrea will never stop fighting to keep it that way.

positions.summary: Endorsed Ballot Question 7, which would allow single-family homes on lots as small as 5,000 square feet where public water and sewer exist.
positions.quote: I am proud to vote Yes on Question 7 and I encourage every Massachusetts voter to do the same.

positions.summary: Her campaign says she sued over the administration's tariffs, which it calls illegal.
positions.quote: Andrea isn’t letting him keep raising prices illegally.

positions.summary: Her campaign describes her litigation blocking federal efforts to compel Massachusetts agencies to cooperate with ICE, and her guide and reporting portal on ICE conduct.
positions.quote: Andrea knows ICE has gone too far.

record.text: Co-led a multistate lawsuit, filed the day after the January 2025 executive order, challenging the order to end birthright citizenship; her campaign says the suit won a nationwide injunction and continued to the U.S. Supreme Court.
Co-led a 25-state coalition suing over a presidential directive involving the Postal Service and mail-in voting; her campaign says a preliminary injunction was won.
Sued five large corporate landlords and the rent-pricing software companies they used, and secured a $7 million multistate settlement, according to her campaign.

Enforced the MBTA Communities Act, which requires communities served by public transit to allow multifamily housing; her campaign says the Supreme Judicial Court rejected Marshfield's challenge to the law.
Secured a settlement with Uber and Lyft providing a $34-per-hour minimum wage, health care and paid family leave for Massachusetts drivers, according to her campaign.

candidates.researchNotes: The Attorney General's own press releases on mass.gov returned HTTP 403 to automated access, so official-action items are cited to her campaign's description rather than to the office's releases; dates were not given for several items.

candidates.name: Michael Walsh
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the September 1, 2026 Republican primary.

priorities.text: Enforcing the legislative audit law: "No selective enforcement. No political shielding."
Protecting local control over zoning, opposing state-imposed zoning mandates tied to funding.
Lowering utility bills by fighting rate increases, and aggressively investigating fraud, waste and abuse.
Stricter vetting of ballot questions for clarity and legality.

statements.quote: Local zoning decisions belong to cities and towns not unelected state bureaucrats.
statements.context: On his campaign website, describing his opposition to state-imposed zoning mandates

candidates.researchNotes: No elected record. His campaign says he is litigating several active cases against the Attorney General's office (legislative audit, public records, MBTA Communities Act); those cases were not independently verified.

researchNotes: Slate from the Elections Division's official primary results (electionstats) and The Green Papers; the Secretary of the Commonwealth's certified general-election list (sec.state.ma.us) is behind a bot-protection block and was not loaded, and Ballotpedia returns a WAF page. The Attorney General's own mass.gov press releases return HTTP 403 to automated access, so Campbell's official-action items are cited to her campaign's description and labeled as such; dates were not given for several items. A news-reported ballot-signature dispute involving Walsh's primary nomination papers was removed because its status (appeals) could not be fully stated. Campaign finance omitted per brief.
